question.knowledge_point: Constructing the Speed-Time Graph for a Real-Life Scenario
question.problem: A particle accelerates from rest with a constant acceleration of $5\,{\text{km/h}}^{2}$ for the first $4$ hours of its motion. It then travels at a constant speed for the next $6$ hours. Which graph represents the described motion?
question.worked_solution:
We start the first line from the point $(0,0),$ since the particle starts from rest. Then, because the acceleration is $5\,{\text{km/h}}^{2},$ we draw a line with slope $5.$ 

However, because the particle is only accelerating for the first $4$ hours, we stop the line at $t=4.$ At this time, the particle's speed has increased by $4\cdot 5=20\text{ km/h}.$ So, the first line segment goes from $(0,0)$ to $(4,20).$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13945962/assets/cf0471f38486963f4237b4fab7c1cd109d02cc2d7ac3e30990831654f04c5b11.png)

The particle then travels at a constant speed for the next $6$ hours. So, the speed remains at $20\,\text{km/h}$ for the next $6$ hours, until $t=4+6=10.$

So, the second line segment stops at the point $(10,20).$ The final graph is

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13945962/assets/fae4c7d8cfc79dd70041ebd697226408a5cdd0676ad2ddfaad1500ea1ba0a76e.png)

judgment.reasoning:
All 16 final answers agree with their own captured Math Academy solutions. The source_error judgment records authored errors in intermediate prose or labels: q-108567 says 'After $t=3,$' although the third segment starts at t=6; q-70903 says the tangent is evaluated at x=1 although its calculation correctly evaluates x=3; q-124475 incorrectly labels the tangent ratio as tan(A), when it is tan(B); q-72768 labels the computed triangle area A_ACD while discussing triangle ACB. None changes the final answer. q-72764 rounds an intermediate area prematurely, but using the unrounded value still gives 19 square centimeters.

For q-59711 and q-108462, using the source's explicit positive-acceleration convention, increasing speed occurs from 0 to 30 seconds and from 30 to 60 seconds, respectively. The decreasing segments represent deceleration, which is also nonzero signed acceleration in physics terminology. For q-59760, v=5t until t=4 gives v=20, followed by constant speed through t=10. For q-108567, the successive graph vertices are (0,0), (3,3), (6,3), and (9,4.5). For q-70903, differentiating the base-10 logarithm gives y'=3/(x ln(10))+3x², hence 27+1/ln(10) at x=3.

For q-28266, (2x+4)/(x-1)=5 gives x=3 and area (2)(10)/2=10. For q-76773, sqrt(3)x/(x+4)=tan(30°) gives x=2 and area 6sqrt(3). For q-124475, 2sqrt(3)x/(x+2)=tan(60°) gives x=2 and area 8sqrt(3).

For q-18688, substitution gives a=1.2 and b=1.4. For q-112561, elimination gives x=-2 and y=3, hence x+y=1. For q-26223, the scaled equations 3x-y=6 and 6x+8y=2 give x=5/3 and y=-1. For q-18720, p=-4q-2 gives q=-4.5 and p=16, hence p+2q=7.

For q-18027, area=22·26·sin(11°)/2≈54.57137, rounding to 54.57. For q-43339, 15=5·12·sin(A)/2 gives sin(A)=1/2; the depicted acute angle selects 30° rather than the supplementary 150°. For q-72768, area=18·8·sin(70°)≈135.31574, rounding to 135. For q-72764, subtracting the concave quadrilateral's area from triangle ABD gives 67.5·sin(52°)-34≈19.19073, rounding to 19.
